chunks: From him, from Al-Hasan ibn Musa al-Khashshab, from Ghiyath ibn Kalloon, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, from Ja'far, from his father (peace be upon them both):
That Ali (peace be upon him) freed a slave of his, so he said to him, 'Indeed, your ownership is mine, but I have left it for you.'
ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say to his slave after freeing him regarding ownership?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the concept of *Iqat* (partial manumission) or a specific form of emancipation where the master retains the legal title (*Milk*) while transferring the usufruct or benefit to the freed slave. It highlights the juristic nuance in Shia fiqh regarding the distinction between ownership rights and the practical benefits of freedom, reflecting Imam Ali’s precise legal reasoning during his caliphate. The narration underscores the generosity of the Ahl al-Bayt in facilitating social mobility while maintaining clear legal boundaries.
